clue.text: Legitimate line thoroughly unpleasant

parts.note: something thoroughly unpleasant is awful

explanation.surface: A rule is within the law yet still deeply disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful conduct is permitted by law, which is what legitimate means.

clue.text: Self-evident statement made by a cross on Irish Sea island

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
IOM abbreviates the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone states the obvious while marking a cross on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a premise accepted as true without needing proof.

clue.text: Moving quickly to confuse bat

parts.note: flying means moving quickly, as in a flying visit
to fox is to confuse or baffle

explanation.surface: Something darting around fast to bewilder a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying fox is a large fruit bat.

clue.text: Primate's capital broadcast

definitions.note: read as 'Primate is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: An archbishop's cathedral city is being announced on air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R is silent, so LEMUR and LIMA are both said LEE-muh.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a tree-dwelling primate from Madagascar.

clue.text: Bar over in parlour

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other here

parts.note: a salon is a parlour or reception room
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A drink served across the counter in someone's front room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside SALON. The cricket abbreviation O for 'over' is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a public room in a pub, or in the Wild West the bar itself.

clue.text: See tiger roaming round northern plain

indicators.note: round means going around, so one piece encloses the other
roaming means wandering about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch a tiger wandering across a northern plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' makes SEREGETI, which 'round' wraps about N. 'plain' is the noun, grassland, not the adjective meaning simple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania and Kenya.

clue.text: A great many besieging uranium plant

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: lots means a great many
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Crowds surround a uranium processing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks industrial next to uranium, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is an aquatic flowering plant, sacred in several Asian religions.

clue.text: Typically old, part of church seen before storm

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: An old church nave is spotted before a storm hits.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means usually or in the normal run of things.

clue.text: Start completely determined

parts.note: out means completely, as in tired out
set means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: Someone starts out thoroughly resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the beginning of something.

clue.text: Steal tin at church

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A thief takes a tin from a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to grab or steal quickly.

clue.text: One close to Nancy, one of the Mitfords

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so this takes the final letter of Nancy

explanation.surface: Someone intimate with Nancy, herself one of the famous Mitford sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is a Mitford too, which makes 'close to Nancy' look like part of the definition; it only supplies the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity Mitford was one of the six celebrated Mitford sisters of interwar English society, alongside the novelist Nancy.

clue.text: Author's record win at swimming

definitions.note: read as 'Author is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: to mark something is to record or note it

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's personal best in a swimming race.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, pen name of Samuel Clemens, wrote Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Discussion group remains uncertain

indicators.note: letters that are uncertain are not fixed in place, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A panel's discussion ends without a settled conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class or meeting where a group discusses a topic.

clue.text: Budding, infinite number with a pleasant smell

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified, indefinitely large number in maths
a scent is a pleasant smell

explanation.surface: Flowers in bud, countless and fragrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, as a budding talent is.

clue.text: Put a stopwatch on game of snooker for a specified period?

parts.note: to time something is to measure it with a stopwatch
a frame is a single game in a snooker match

explanation.surface: Timing a snooker frame to see how long it takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeframe is the stretch of time allotted for something to happen.

clue.text: Actor from Maine beginning to learn on American guitar

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of learn

parts.note: Gibson is a US guitar maker, famous for the Les Paul

explanation.surface: A performer from Maine starts learning to play an American guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel Gibson is the Australian-American star of Mad Max and Braveheart.

clue.text: Without any complications in Naples and at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smooth voyage in the Bay of Naples and out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Going as planned means happening exactly as intended, with no hitches.

clue.text: Book reckless forward

parts.note: rash means reckless

explanation.surface: Reserve a reckless player for the forward line.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is bold and presumptuous, which is what brash describes.

clue.text: Last drink, so here's to you!

parts.note: the bottom is the last place, as in bottom of the league
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A final round with a toast to the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a toast urging everyone to drain their glasses, like cheers.

clue.text: Garden plants in clusters, from what we hear

indicators.note: this tells us the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: flocks are clusters or crowds

explanation.surface: Garden flowers that grow in clusters, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a genus of flowering border plants grown in gardens.

clue.text: To eat out is an easy thing to do

definitions.meaning: a ... is informally something easy, as in 'it's no ...'

explanation.surface: Dining outdoors is effortless.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means eating al fresco; the noun is a casual phrase for an easy task.

clue.text: Going nowhere, like a team that's lost every match?

definitions.meaning: something going nowhere is futile, without purpose

definitions.text: like a team that's lost every match?
definitions.meaning: a team losing every match scores no points

explanation.surface: A hopeless team that keeps losing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: the question mark flags 'without points' as a literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile effort is pointless; a winless team is literally without points.

clue.text: Band in street on right

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next, so street comes first

parts.note: ripe means right or ready, as in the time is ripe

explanation.surface: A band playing in a street on the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour.

clue.text: Fabled monster in rhyme, tailless rat

parts.note: to chime is to rhyme or harmonise

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of rat is dropped

explanation.surface: A mythical beast appears in a verse alongside a rat with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing creature, part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Blunder made by troublesome child forgetting time

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A naughty child makes a gaffe, losing track of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Clothing Australian's mate left inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Clothes an Australian's friend has left behind indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British slang for clothes or gear.

clue.text: Explicit about writer of nonsense verse

parts.note: C abbreviates circa, Latin for about
Edward Lear wrote The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: Plain-spoken remarks on a nonsense poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear is plain and unambiguous, which explicit means.

clue.text: Nerve of supporters on top of stand

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, here of stand

explanation.surface: Fans in the top tier of the stand show plenty of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' suggests fans, but they are underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal for cheek or nerve, as in brass neck.

clue.text: Awful nuisance engaging bouncer, ultimately for protection

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so one piece holds the other
awful suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess, so they are reordered
ultimately points to the final letter of bouncer

explanation.surface: A club hires a bouncer to guard against a dreadful pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges NUISANCE into INSUANCE, and 'engaging' takes in R, the last letter of bouncer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is cover that protects against loss or harm.

clue.text: Onset of storm affected little monkey

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so this takes the first letter of storm

parts.note: camp means affected or theatrically exaggerated

explanation.surface: A small monkey is upset by the start of a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a scamp or, playfully, a little monkey.

clue.text: Girl riding, changing ends

indicators.note: the front and back portions of the word riding swap places

explanation.surface: A girl on horseback switches ends of the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ends' moves RID from the front of RIDING to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a girl's name, as in Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Extremely reasonable late meal

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so this takes the first and last letters of reasonable

parts.note: late can mean former, past

explanation.surface: A late-night meal at a fair hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.
